purpose: Nilutamide is used to treat prostate cancer in men. It is typically used together with a surgical procedure called orchiectomy (removal of the testicles) to help stop the cancer from growing. By blocking male hormones, it helps slow down or stop the spread of prostate cancer cells.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells need male hormones called androgens (like testosterone) to grow. Nilutamide works by blocking the places on cancer cells where testosterone tries to attach, kind of like putting a plug in a lock so the key cannot get in. Without being able to use testosterone, the cancer cells cannot grow as easily.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include hot flashes, decreased sex drive, nausea, dizziness, trouble seeing in the dark or adjusting from bright to dim light (called visual adaptation problems), mild constipation, and feeling tired. Some men may notice mild swelling or tenderness in the chest area.
warnings: Important: Nilutamide can rarely cause serious lung problems (like pneumonia-type inflammation) — tell your doctor right away if you develop shortness of breath or a new cough. It can also cause liver problems, so your doctor will check your liver with blood tests. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can cause a serious reaction including flushing, low blood pressure, and nausea. Always tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as nilutamide can interact with several drugs including blood thinners.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 300 mg (three 100 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day for the first 30 days. After that, the dose is reduced to 150 mg (one and a half 100 mg tablets) once daily. It is best to take it at the same time each day, with or without food. Always follow exactly what your doctor prescribes.
